# Supermatter Stability
The Supermatter continuously monitors its own structural stability.
When stability falls below safe operating levels, the crystal automatically broadcasts warnings to the station's engineering radio network.
Stability is influenced by the environment surrounding the crystal. Engineers should continuously monitor chamber conditions and respond to any unexpected changes.
## Sources of Stress
Any process that introduces additional energy into the crystal may reduce its structural stability.
Based on current Nanotrasen operating guidelines, Engineering personnel are advised to keep chamber conditions within the following recommended operating ranges whenever practical:
- Temperatures below approximately 350 K - Chamber pressures between approximately 50 kPa and 250 kPa
Additional sources of structural stress include:
- Emitter shots - Laser impacts - Physical contact with the crystal
Operating outside these recommendations does not necessarily result in immediate instability, but prolonged or extreme deviations have been associated with accelerated structural degradation.
## Chamber Conditions
The atmosphere surrounding the crystal plays a major role in maintaining stability.
Engineers should continuously monitor:
- Temperature - Pressure - Atmospheric composition
Standard station atmospheric conditions have consistently provided a reliable operating environment.
Significant changes should only be performed after careful planning.
## Improving Stability
Proper chamber design improves the crystal's tolerance to changing operating conditions.
Cooling systems connected directly to the chamber should include overpressure countermeasures.
Pressure regulators can be connected to the cooling loop and chamber to limit excessive pressure buildup.
Additional inlet valves provide further protection by allowing pressure to be controlled at multiple points within the system.
Higher-capacity cooling systems may also be installed.
Hellfire Freezers provide increased cooling capacity, allowing the system to remove heat more effectively and maintain the chamber closer to the desired operating temperature during high-stress operation.
